data.description:
## The defect

The MCP server resolves commits against its own code clone at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`. That
clone is not fetched before a completion precheck, so it can lag `origin/main`. When it does, a close
routed through MCP for work whose commit HAS merged is refused with "no commit references it" — the
precheck cannot see a commit that demonstrably exists.

Observed 2026-09-05 while closing `5310-b51f-bba6-4e61`: the MCP path could not resolve the merged
SHAs and refused the close. The agent did NOT force it. It fell back to the local `rebar` CLI from a
worktree that provably contained the commits, and the same close passed — which is sound, because the
precheck is explicitly a worktree-HEAD reachability check and the local worktree satisfied it
honestly.

## Why this matters more than a one-off annoyance

AGENTS.md directs agents to route tracker operations THROUGH the MCP server, with the local CLI as
the carve-out for local-code ops. So the documented primary path is the one that fails, and it fails
precisely on the most common case: closing a ticket shortly after its change merges. The refusal
message names the ticket's evidence ("no commit references it") rather than the server's own staleness,
so it reads as a defect in the work rather than in the resolver — which invites exactly the wrong
response.

The correct fallback exists and worked here, but it depends on the agent knowing that the local CLI
is legitimate for this and that the refusal was not about their commit. An agent that believed the
refusal would either re-push, re-verify, or reach for a bypass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The MCP server's commit resolution cannot silently use a stale clone: either it fetches before
      resolving, or it detects staleness and says so. State which and why.
- [ ] A refusal caused by the server being unable to SEE a commit is distinguishable in its message
      from a refusal caused by no commit referencing the ticket. The two are different conditions and
      currently render identically.
- [ ] Defect-seeded: with the clone deliberately behind a merged commit, confirm the new behaviour
      (fetch-then-resolve, or an explicit staleness error) rather than the misleading refusal. An
      unobserved fix is not evidence.
- [ ] The legitimate local-CLI fallback is documented where an agent hitting this will find it, so the
      recovery does not depend on someone having seen it before.
- [ ] Portability: no dependence on any single CI provider trigger.

## Testing

1. RED first: put the clone behind a merged commit and reproduce the current misleading refusal.
2. Confirm a genuinely unreferenced ticket still refuses, with its own distinct message — the fix must
   not make the real condition unreportable.
3. Confirm a current clone still closes normally.

## Provenance

Found by an agent closing three merged tickets on 2026-09-05. It reported the refusal, declined to
force, and used the sanctioned fallback — so no damage resulted, but only because it reasoned
correctly about a message that pointed the wrong way.
data.title: The MCP server's code clone goes stale, so MCP-routed closes of recently-merged work refuse with "no commit references it"
